scope: Reaper systems language, reference runtime, native C17 track, Studio, LSP/DAP and explicit local integrations.

reference.warning: The supplied 66-point list mixes cumulative updates, inherited behavior, absence statements, repeated topics and Windows-specific constraints. It is not treated as an authoritative XP SP3 changelog or as a requirement to reproduce legacy Windows behavior.

adoption_rules.rule: Only claim implemented when repository code and tests or operational evidence support the exact behavior. Partial requires evidence and explicit limits. Not applicable requires a product-scope reason. Historical Windows features are not silently represented as native capabilities.

source_groups.title: User interface, shell, multimedia and storage

controls.assessment: The reference runtime has execution quotas and explicit host-effect boundaries; native hardware services and complete type/ownership/effect enforcement remain partial.
limitations: Native code and hardware adapters must stay opt-in and bounded.

controls.assessment: Reaper is a local developer tool; its LSP/DAP use stdio and network services or remote execution are not part of the current product scope.
limitations: Do not add network services merely to imitate Windows networking features.

controls.assessment: The Python package, local toolchain discovery and desktop build workflows exist; a signed system installer and OS-level servicing framework are not claimed.
limitations: Keep package installation separate from privileged system updates.

controls.assessment: Studio, CLI and local project/source handling exist; a system-wide shell, compositor and OS storage manager are outside scope.
limitations: UI capability claims must remain scoped to the desktop IDE.

controls.assessment: The Python runtime remains the compatibility reference while the C17 backend is partial; language, ABI and example checks cover only documented contracts.
limitations: Do not equate compatibility with full backend or hardware-runtime parity.
